findings.detail: An inherited snapshot context can identify the wrong producing bundle. For example, use snapshot A's exec command to invoke a checked-gate from complete bundle B. B's startup verifies A's snapshot and identity, but never checks that its own executable and checked_core.py belong to A. B then reads HELPER_BUNDLE_IDENTITY from the environment and can render A's receipt or stamp new evidence as A. This defeats the new refusal of another producing bundle without modifying any manifest.
findings.evidence: helper-snapshot.environment preserves the identity through arbitrary subprocesses. check_invocation at lines 138-141 compares two descriptions of the environment-selected snapshot without comparing the executing bundle's location or inventory. checked-gate:20-21 and checked-plant:20-21 call that check; checked_core.py:31-50 returns the inherited identity instead of describing the executing bundle. require_helper_bundle consequently accepts A's evidence while B's code is running.
findings.title: Uncited: Unenforced trust boundary: bind inherited identity to the executing bundle

findings.detail: The documented review-until-clean integration with review-pr-with-codex no longer has a shared repository snapshot identifier. Each skill must snapshot its own plugin, so hashing helper_bundle makes otherwise identical captures differ by plugin name, version and bundle hash. When the reviewer echoes its reviewed snapshot, the loop must reject it as another snapshot even though repository inputs have not changed. Preserve producer identity while providing a repository-input identity or an explicit comparison contract for this composition.
findings.evidence: Both maintained review-scope files now hash helper_bundle at lines 651-659. review-until-clean/SKILL.md documents /review-pr-with-codex as a reviewer and rejects an echoed value that is not the round's value. Its references/reviewers.md:57 explicitly requires that match. review-pr-with-codex independently captures scope and sets each aspect's reviewed value to its own snapshot. The two plugin manifests necessarily supply different bundle names.
findings.title: Uncited: Parallel paths: producer-bound scope hashes break the documented reviewer composition

findings.detail: The new opening rule requires verified snapshot invocations, but the helper section still directs the agent to invoke the installed cache path with Bash, find it using a version-blind glob, and reuse that absolute path for the session. Following those concrete steps bypasses verification and leaves later captures, completion checks and ledger publication dependent on the removable cache. Replace the old helper-resolution instructions and abbreviations with the snapshot launcher, as the sibling review-pr-with-codex skill does.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:10 requires helpers only through the verified launcher. Lines 47-58 instead prescribe bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/review-scope", a **/review-until-clean/**/scripts/review-scope search, and reuse of that installed path for all three helpers. review-anti-patterns/references/edit-mode.md:11 also directs its dependency lookup to this helper section. The branch updates the equivalent section in review-pr-with-codex but leaves this path unchanged.
findings.title: Uncited: Agent-prose control flow: remove instructions that still invoke cache helpers directly

findings.detail: The recommended permission examples still describe direct Bash helper invocations after the workflow moves to uv run --script through helper-snapshot. In particular, the claim that the first two rules cover the bundled scope helper is now inaccurate. The same stale Bash helper rules remain in the review-pr-with-codex and review-anti-patterns READMEs. Update the examples and explanations to describe the new invocation and any approvals intentionally left manual.
findings.evidence: review-until-clean/README.md:112 permits Bash(bash "*/review-scope" ...), and line 119 says those rules cover the helper. The shared snapshot reference instead invokes uv run --script "${launcher}" run .... review-pr-with-codex/README.md and review-anti-patterns/README.md likewise retain direct Bash helper permission entries.
findings.title: Uncited: Docs drift: refresh permission examples for the snapshot launcher
